teams.heading: Maro Itoje claims summer sabbatical was 'wise' decision for England career
teams.body: Maro Itoje has defended the decision to skip England’s summer schedule, admitting Steve Borthwick's proposal for a sabbatical initially took him by surprise. Having surpassed the 2,400-minute player load threshold in successive seasons, the captain sat out July's matches against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina to prioritise mental recovery following the death of his mother. Itoje, who has won 102 caps, told reporters: "It was a wise and prudent decision, it has given me the best opportunity to perform well."

teams.heading: Former Ireland lock Ryan Caldwell reveals recovery from addiction and incarceration
teams.body: Former Ireland and Ulster second-row Ryan Caldwell has candidly detailed his descent into addiction, imprisonment, and suicidal depression following his retirement from professional rugby. Speaking ahead of his autobiography, White Lines, the 42-year-old described how the transition from the enforcer role at clubs like Bath and Exeter led to a spiral of mental health struggles. Now a meditation teacher in Belfast, Caldwell credits breathwork and meditation for his recovery, offering a raw perspective on the mental health challenges facing retired professionals.

teams.body: Italy lock Andrea Zambonin is ruled out of the start of the Premiership season as he recovers from a shoulder injury. teams.heading: Scottish Rugby expresses surprise as Sione Fukofuka joins Australia after resignation
teams.body: Scottish Rugby officials have been left stunned after former women’s head coach Sione Fukofuka was unveiled as Australia’s new boss just days after his resignation. Fukofuka stepped down in August citing "family stress" and personal reasons, leaving the national side without a permanent lead ahead of this month’s WXV series at Hive Stadium. While Glasgow Warriors Women’s coach Robbie Fergusson recently joined that club programme, a permanent national successor is yet to be named. The union’s public surprise at the rapid Australian appointment adds significant tension to the vacancy.

teams.heading: Wigan Warriors to host funeral for Wales icon Sir Billy Boston
teams.body: The funeral for Welsh rugby great Sir Billy Boston will take place on 10 September at The Brick Community Stadium, home of Wigan Warriors. The Cardiff-born legend passed away last week at the age of 92, just days after the funeral of his wife, Lady Joan. Fans are invited to pay their respects along the funeral cortege route in Wigan before the service, which will be live-streamed for those unable to attend the limited-capacity ceremony.

teams.heading: Argentina XV records dominant victory against Uruguay XV in regional championship
teams.body: The Argentina XV secured a 64-10 win over the Uruguay XV in the second round of the 2026 Americas Rugby Championship. The side scored 10 tries, including a hat-trick from Luciano Avaca. Franco Rossetto added two tries, with further scores coming from Felipe Villagrán, Bautista Estellés, Tomás Dande, Rodrigo Fernández Criado, and Sebastián Pérez. The team will conclude their tournament campaign against the Chile XV.

teams.heading: Les Kiss faces scrutiny as Wallabies adopt forward-heavy attacking system
teams.body: Australia’s reliance on their forward pack has prompted questions regarding the team’s long-term identity as they prepare for next year’s World Cup. Under Les Kiss, 73 per cent of the side’s 34 tries this year have been scored by forwards, a trend the head coach described as "clunky" following the win in Jujuy. While this approach has helped secure four consecutive victories, critics suggest the system restricts backline opportunities, leaving the squad vulnerable to teams capable of neutralising their dominant set-piece.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One grants international veterans special registration status
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has revised its controversial player registration system following a legal settlement with 25 players, including high-profile international stars like Timothy Lafaele and Jiwon Gu. Under the updated framework, players who have earned 30 or more caps for the Brave Blossoms will now be reclassified from Category A-2 to Category A-1. This concession effectively resolves the discrimination dispute that had threatened to disrupt the upcoming 2026-2027 season via a Tokyo District Court injunction.

teams.heading: Daan Human rejects All Blacks claims as Springboks prepare for Soweto
teams.body: Springboks assistant coach Daan Human has hit back at accusations from All Blacks boss Dave Rennie regarding scrum tactics ahead of Saturday’s third Test. Rennie previously alleged the South African pack were 'walking around' to gain an advantage, a claim Human emphatically denied. "I can't ever cheat or tell the players to walk around – we never work like that," Human insisted. With the series level at 1-1, the focus shifts to Soweto as both sides look to move past the set-piece controversy.
